title: An Absorbing State Model with an Emergent Ising Transition
authors: Shen Ai, Dov Levine, Paul Chaikin
abstract: We study a dynamical model of repulsive needles with centers fixed on a square lattice. Needles that overlap are active and receive a repulsive rotation $ θ\in [0,ε)$; needles with no overlap do not move. This model exhibits an absorbing state transition. Nematic order was observed for long needles. For a range of needle lengths and $ε$, the system self-organizes into a state with checkerboard symmetry. As $ε$ is increased, this phase melts and becomes disordered. Remarkably, we find that this phase boundary exhibits critical exponents identical to those of the equilibrium 2D Ising model.
summary: This work analyzes a dynamical model of repulsive needles on a lattice, which exhibits multiple phase transitions. The most notable finding is that the transition between ordered and disordered active states belongs to the 2D Ising universality class. The study rigorously confirms this using finite-size scaling and demonstrates that the system operates far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The study investigates phase transitions in a non-equilibrium, dynamical model of repulsive needles, specifically focusing on the emergence of Ising critical behavior in an ordering transition.
main_result: The system exhibits two transitions: an absorbing/active transition and an ordering transition between active phases, where the latter displays critical exponents identical to the 2D Ising model.
method: The analysis employs dynamical simulations, finite-size scaling, and the calculation of non-equilibrium quantities like entropy production to characterize the phase boundaries and critical behavior.
model_or_system: The model consists of repulsive needles fixed on a 2D square lattice. Dynamics are driven by synchronous, repulsive rotations ($\epsilon$ kick size) when needles overlap, leading to active states.
key_observables: Fraction of active particles ($f_a$), local and global CB order parameters ($m$), susceptibility, and correlation length.
important_parameters: Kick size ($\epsilon$), needle length ($2r$), and lattice geometry (square lattice).
main_assumptions: The system is fundamentally out of equilibrium, as evidenced by non-zero entropy production, and the Ising symmetry is emergent from the lattice geometry rather than inherent spin symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams mapping the three identified phases, finite-size scaling confirming 2D Ising exponents, and time evolution showing linear decay of domain size squared ($R^2 \propto -Kt$).
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the phase diagram in parameter space, first identifying the absorbing/active transition, and then focusing on the upper ordering transition, which is characterized by scaling analysis and coarsening dynamics.
why_interesting: The emergence of classical critical behavior (Ising universality) from a purely kinetic, non-equilibrium system driven by steric repulsion is a rich topic for understanding how symmetry can be imposed by geometry in complex many-body dynamics.
